topic: How does ECRA's MRC SINR model influence transponder linearity requirements in high-interference scenarios?
consensus_response: ECRA's MRC SINR model amplifies interference by combining replicas weighted by their root mean squared received signal level, degrading array factor and instantaneous mutual information. In high-interference scenarios, this leads to a degradation of the signal-to-interference ratio (SINR) at the output of the combiner. As a result, transponder linearity requirements are influenced by the increased SINR, necessitating more stringent linearity requirements to maintain optimal performance and prevent distortion of amplified signals. The non-linearity of transponders introduces additional interference terms, degrading instantaneous mutual information and requiring a significant increase in replicas to maintain the desired SINR threshold.
reference_context: ECRA's MRC SINR model amplifies interference by combining replicas weighted by their root mean squared received signal level, leading to a degradation of array factor and instantaneous mutual information. This necessitates more stringent linearity requirements for transponders in high-interference scenarios.
